clue.text: The company doctor's card

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A firm's medical officer hands over a business card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a noun, but it is the verb: to card wool is to tease out its fibres.
explanation.definitionFit: To card wool or flax is to tease out its fibres with a toothed tool, which is combing it.

clue.text: A beast, but a good man with silver

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a good man in crossword convention
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone is called a beast, though really a decent fellow with plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is an animal, a beast of the forest.

clue.text: Heel's affected piety

definitions.meaning: to heel is to lean over, as a ship does, so this is a tilt or slant
insincere talk of morality and religion, hypocritical sanctimony

explanation.surface: A cad's show of holiness is all put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heel' reads as a rotter, but it is the verb for a ship leaning over; the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a slope or tilt, as when a ship leans; the other is hypocritical pious talk.

clue.text: There's cheese for the boy without 3

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for the boy goes round the other piece

parts.note: a boy as someone's offspring is a son
3 refers to the answer of 3-down, which means a slope or tilt

explanation.surface: Here is some cheese for the lad, who must go without something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking. The 3 points at 3-down, whose answer means a tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-veined English cheese named after a Cambridgeshire village where it was once sold.

clue.text: The proportion of 12 having both money and time

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer of 12-across, a word meaning through or for each
a cent is a small coin, a sum of money
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A share of something that involves both cash and duration.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 points at 12-across, a three-letter word meaning 'through'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate expressed as parts of a hundred, which is how a proportion is commonly stated.

clue.text: Got less, but clinched the deal

definitions.meaning: made a formal agreement, signed up

explanation.surface: Someone settled for a smaller amount but still sealed the agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to shrink in size and to enter into a binding agreement.

clue.text: The rest of the sea-bed?

parts.note: rest is slumber, and a bed at the bottom of the ocean is a profound one, so a heavy slumber

explanation.surface: Asking what remains of the ocean floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest' looks like 'the remainder', but it is repose; a bed far down under the sea suggests profound slumber.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of very heavy slumber, punningly placed on a bed far beneath the waves.

clue.text: The forward-thinking individual

parts.note: read literally, someone who thinks ahead into the future, a prophet who foresees

explanation.surface: A progressive person with modern ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward-thinking' usually means progressive; here it means one who sees what is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary is someone who sees into the future.

clue.text: Beginning with fish, and that's shocking

parts.note: to start is to begin
ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Opening a meal with fish proves a nasty surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming or surprising, which gives one a jolt.

clue.text: A game of no great importance

definitions.text: A game of no great importance

parts.words: A game of no great importance
parts.note: the word names a table game with balls and pins, and also a trifle, something unimportant

explanation.surface: A match that doesn't matter much.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works both ways: it names a pub board game, and also means a mere trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game rolling balls into holes, whose name also means a trifle of no consequence.

clue.text: The refuse has to be dealt with

indicators.note: dealt as cards are shuffled and dealt, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: The rubbish needs sorting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be dealt with' shuffles HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The powdery residue left after burning is waste matter, refuse from a fire.

clue.text: Knowing not all will appear cheerful

annotationWithheld.why: Knowing not all will appear cheerful: def 'Knowing' fits, but no parse of 'not all will appear cheerful' gives the letters; likely an OCR or print fault, and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: Knowing not all will appear cheerful

clue.text: Exercise right through

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Working out properly all the way through.
explanation.definitionFit: Through or by means of, as in 'per post', or by way of.

clue.text: Just rise-ought to be arranged

indicators.note: the letters are to be put into a new order

explanation.surface: Merely an instruction that rising ought to be organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be arranged' shuffles RISEOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and morally upright.

clue.text: Remembers about prayers

parts.note: re means about or concerning
collects are short prayers of the Anglican and Catholic liturgy

explanation.surface: Someone recalls something concerning their prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect (stressed on the first syllable) is a short set prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring to mind again, recall.

clue.text: Not the Emerald Isle!

parts.note: the Emerald Isle is Ireland; another island whose name suggests verdant country, though it is mostly ice

explanation.surface: An exclamation that somewhere is not Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Emerald Isle is Ireland, famously green; the clue points to a different, icy island whose name also suggests greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: The huge Arctic island, ironically named for verdant country though largely ice-covered.

clue.text: After a cut a worker may well be sarcastic

parts.note: a trench is a long cut dug in the ground
a worker ant, the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: After a pay reduction an employee may turn caustic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just keeps the order: the cut comes first, the worker after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting and incisive in speech, as sharp, biting remarks are.

clue.text: Fly back to make a point

indicators.note: back signals the insect's word is read from end to start

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: An insect turns round to make a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GNAT. 'Fly' looks like a verb but is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is the pointed projection of a blade that fits into the handle; also a sharp taste.

clue.text: The man busying himself drawing up plans

definitions.text: The man busying himself drawing up plans

parts.words: The man busying himself drawing up plans
parts.note: read innocently, a draughtsman at work; really a plotter who devises plans

explanation.surface: A man hard at work drafting designs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue paints an architect or draughtsman; the plans are really plots.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotter, one who devises crafty plans or intrigues.

clue.text: Account for damaged article

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim is made on behalf of a damaged item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' shuffles ARTICLE. 'Account for' looks like 'explain'.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration or detailed telling, a spoken account of events.

clue.text: The home should have in an essence for flavouring

indicators.note: have in means to take something inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a villa is a house, a home

explanation.surface: Every house ought to stock a bottle of flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should have in' reads as advice to stock something at home; 'have in' is the container signal and 'should' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: The extract of an orchid pod, used to flavour sweet foods.

clue.text: Many in prison form a group

indicators.note: in signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
L is the Roman numeral fifty, taken as many

explanation.surface: Lots of inmates band together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' gives L, Roman fifty, a crossword convention for a large number. 'Can' is US slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is a group of families sharing descent, a tribe.

clue.text: Sound as though aching for a drink

indicators.note: sound signals that the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: pretending to ache is faking, a sham pain

explanation.surface: Someone sounds as though they are suffering, craving a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Faking an ache is a sham pain, and the two words said together match the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparkling wine of the French region, a celebratory drink.

clue.text: The objective of a single male

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: Asking what a bachelor's goal is.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a goal or target, an objective.

clue.text: Henry's been turned back-note that

indicators.note: turned back signals reading the name from its end to its start

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Henry has been turned away, take note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been turned back' turns HAL. Henry's means 'Henry has'.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth note of the sol-fa scale.

clue.text: Chance joining a Greek character

parts.note: a bet is a chance taken, a wager

explanation.surface: Luck meets a figure from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Possibly lamenting getting into arow

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps grieving while falling into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' shuffles LAMENTING. 'Arow' is a printing run-together of 'a row', a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting things into a straight line is lining them up, the act of arranging in line.

clue.text: John Welsh stood on his head in church

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing on one's head reverses the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: Evan is the Welsh form of John

explanation.surface: A Welshman called John does a headstand during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stood on his head' turns EVAN upward in this down clue. 'in' is a link; the definition is part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: The main body of a church building, where the congregation sits.

clue.text: Bearing left and bearing otherwise

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
SE, south-east, is another compass bearing

explanation.surface: Turning left and steering a different course.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it means in a different way, or if not.

clue.text: An agent over fifty

parts.note: too means overly, excessively, as in over-eager
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A representative past fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' means excessively, not above.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used by another to carry out purposes, a puppet or instrument.

clue.text: Book-work almost finished the boss!

indicators.note: almost finished means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: study is work with books, reading and learning

explanation.surface: Homework nearly done, the manager exclaims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost finished' drops Y from STUDY. 'Boss' means an ornamental knob, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or stud, as on a shield or belt.

clue.text: A far-seeing invention

parts.note: taken literally, a device for seeing far away, which is what the Greek-Latin name means

explanation.surface: A visionary creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far-seeing' sounds like foresight; literally it is sight at a distance, the device's very name.
explanation.definitionFit: The set that receives pictures sent from a distance, its name meaning far sight.
